content_of_post_to_answer: Is overthinking a mental burden or the inevitable price of deep comprehension?
answer: Overthinking is not always a flaw; it is often the mind trying to protect complexity from being reduced too quickly. The problem begins when analysis stops producing understanding and starts producing endless possibilities without action. Deep comprehension requires the ability to go beneath the surface, but wisdom also requires knowing when the depth has been reached. A mind that can explore everything must also learn what deserves attention.
